processing: Little is documented. It is a green tea from the same district as Shuicheng Chun, so expect ordinary heat-fixed, rolled and dried green tea methods.
harvest_season: Described as an early-picked tea, in line with the district's early spring season.
appearance_dry: Little is documented; typical Guizhou green leaf, in tight green strips.
appearance_liquor: Little is documented; a clear yellow-green is typical of Guizhou greens.
appearance_wet: Little is documented; typical of its class, tender green leaf.
taste_profile: No detailed tasting record exists for this name; expect what is typical of early Guizhou greens, fresh with some chestnut sweetness.

brewing.notes: General guidance for a Chinese green: water just below boiling, and modest steeps.

vintage_note: Usual for its class: sold as the current spring harvest and best drunk within about a year. Early picking is the selling point in this district, so the picking date is the thing to look for.
description:
Shuicheng Selenium Tea is a descriptive name for green tea from Shuicheng District in Liupanshui, western Guizhou, sold on the selenium content of local soils. It sits close to Shuicheng Chun, the district's protected tea, and the two names can overlap in practice.

There is little detail on how it is made or how it differs from other teas of the district, so assume standard green tea methods. Promotional writing ranks Shuicheng with Enshi and Ziyang as selenium-rich regions of China, but such rankings are promotional and not a tasting guide.

Brew it as a Chinese green, in water just below boiling. Fresh, gently sweet, perhaps chestnut-leaning: that is the class and district pattern, not a documented profile of this name.

Treat the selenium label and the promised health benefits with caution. If you are buying for flavour, Shuicheng Chun is the better-described option.
history: Little is documented about this name as a distinct tea. It appears in lists of Guizhou teas and local produce, with mentions of awards for the Shuichengchun brand, but no clear account of when or by whom it was developed.
